flow.title: Atalaya
flow.subtitle: One incident, four products. Replays the asserted end-to-end run: a stalled pipeline is detected, the risky feature is switched off, the on-call team is notified, everything is restored on recovery, and Bitácora drafts the postmortem.
steps: Orders pipeline stalls: backlog 200, oldest message 10 min, consumer has 0 invocations.
Nimbus sees two degraded windows and opens an incident (consumer_stalled).
Nimbus calls Flagship with an HMAC-signed request: orders-v2 goes OFF, audited as nimbus (automation).
Flagship streams the change over SSE: your services take the safe path 680 ms after the observation.
Nimbus notifies Hookrelay. The idempotency key makes a retried call harmless.
Hookrelay delivers a signed incident.opened webhook to the on-call endpoint, with retries and a DLQ behind it.
The pipeline is healthy for two windows: Nimbus marks the incident recovered.
Flagship restores orders-v2, because nobody changed it during the incident.
Hookrelay delivers incident.recovered. Loop closed: detect, mitigate, notify, recover.
Bitácora, subscribed through Hookrelay, rebuilds the timeline (mitigated in 677 ms) and drafts the postmortem.

atalaya.title: Atalaya — Developer Infrastructure Platform
atalaya.description: Four independent products that close the loop detect → mitigate → notify → recover → learn: Nimbus watches AWS async pipelines, Flagship controls features with kill switches, Hookrelay delivers events reliably, and Bitácora turns each incident into a timeline and a postmortem. Integrated only through signed, idempotent HTTP APIs.

highlights.label: End-to-end, asserted
highlights.text: A stalled pipeline in Nimbus turns a flag off in Flagship (SDKs see it in 680 ms), Hookrelay notifies the customer webhook and Bitácora drafts the postmortem; recovery restores everything.

highlights.label: Built to fail safely
highlights.text: HMAC-signed calls with a replay window, idempotent on every hop, and humans win over automation: a flag edited during the incident is never overwritten.

highlights.label: Production-shaped
highlights.text: Hexagonal cores, OpenTelemetry + Prometheus/Grafana, k6-measured, Playwright E2E, Terraform on AWS (ECS for the services, Lambda + DynamoDB for Bitácora), GitHub Actions with OIDC, CodeQL/Trivy clean.

atalaya.detailedDescription:
Atalaya (Spanish for watchtower) is a developer infrastructure platform made of four products, each with its own repository, database and pipeline, each useful alone.

Hookrelay is webhook delivery as a service: idempotent ingestion, fan-out, Standard Webhooks signatures, retries with jitter, circuit breaker, a dead-letter queue with bulk replay, and SSRF protection enforced at connection time. Flagship is feature management with local evaluation: a TypeScript SDK downloads the ruleset once, evaluates in about 1 µs, and receives changes over a stream fanned out across replicas with PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY. Nimbus is a guardian for AWS asynchronous pipelines (SQS, Lambda, DLQ) written in Go: explainable detectors, deduplicated incidents and a durable workflow engine on PostgreSQL leases. Bitácora is the incident ledger, serverless on AWS (API Gateway, Lambda, DynamoDB): it subscribes to Hookrelay, rebuilds each incident's timeline from events published by different products, measures time to mitigate and recover, and drafts the postmortem.

Together they automate an incident: Nimbus detects a stalled consumer and runs a response workflow whose steps call Flagship (kill the risky feature flag) and Hookrelay (notify customer systems). When the pipeline recovers, the flag is restored to its pre-incident configuration, unless a person changed it in the meantime, and Bitácora records the whole response. The whole scenario runs locally with one Docker Compose file and a script that asserts every step.
challenges: Joining three products without coupling them: no shared database, queue or code, and no product allowed to depend on another being up.
All three deliver at-least-once, so a retried step could kill a flag twice or notify twice.
Letting automation change production behaviour without it ever fighting a person who is handling the incident.
Rebuilding one timeline from two publishers whose events arrive out of order, more than once, and later than they happened.
solutions: Integration through public HTTP endpoints authenticated by HMAC signatures over the raw body, each one behind an environment variable that turns it off.
Made every hop idempotent: Flagship answers "already off", Hookrelay returns the original message for the same incident key.
Flagship restores a flag only when the latest audit entry is still that incident's kill; otherwise it leaves the flag alone and says why. Covered by integration tests.

Bitácora writes idempotently (keys include the webhook id, timestamps use if_not_exists) and orders events by the source time Nimbus now stamps (occurredAt). The end-to-end demo is what caught that delivery time put "opened" after "mitigated".

kuntur-core-banking.title: Kuntur — Multi-Tenant Core Banking
kuntur-core-banking.description: A core banking platform for credit unions and fintechs: one deployment serves many isolated institutions, books money on a double-entry ledger, speaks ISO 20022 and scores every payment in real time with an explainable risk engine.

highlights.label: Money is correct
highlights.text: Double-entry ledger where the database refuses overdrafts; 20 concurrent transfers against a balance that affords 10 → exactly 10 succeed.

highlights.label: Regulated-grade security
highlights.text: Row-level security per tenant, 28 granular permissions, TOTP MFA and four-eyes approval with step-up, tamper-evident audit hash chain.

highlights.label: Measured and tested
highlights.text: 150 transfers/s at p95 14 ms (k6); 128 backend tests with Testcontainers, 15 Playwright E2E, OWASP ZAP in CI.

kuntur-core-banking.detailedDescription:
Kuntur (Kichwa for the Andean condor) is a multi-tenant core banking platform built the way a regulated system has to be. Payments go through idempotent intake, real-time risk scoring over gRPC and double-entry booking, with a transactional outbox publishing domain events to Kafka. Customers and staff get live updates over WebSocket.

It implements ISO 20022 messages (pain.001/002, pacs.008, camt.053), loans with amortization schedules and automatic installment collection at the end-of-day close, and four-eyes approval with a fresh MFA code for high-value operations. Tenancy is enforced twice: in the application and underneath by PostgreSQL row-level security, with the app running as a role that owns nothing.
challenges: Guaranteeing money is never created or lost under concurrency and crashes.
Isolating institutions so that even a raw SQL mistake cannot cross tenants.
Keeping latency low while every transfer is authenticated, risk-scored and audited.
solutions: Database-enforced invariants (no overdraft), ordered locking, idempotent booking and a recovery sweep, all covered by concurrency tests on real PostgreSQL and Kafka.
Row-level security with a per-transaction tenant, on top of application-level checks.
Measured with k6 end to end (p95 14 ms at 150 transfers/s) and documented the trade-offs, such as keeping virtual threads off because of pinning.

nexus-messenger.title: Nexus Messenger — Real-Time Team Messaging
nexus-messenger.description: A real-time messaging platform with direct and group conversations, presence, typing indicators, file sharing and 1:1 voice and video calls over WebRTC, built on Angular signals and Laravel Reverb WebSockets.

highlights.label: Real-time core
highlights.text: Messages, presence and typing events are broadcast over Laravel Reverb WebSockets and consumed with Laravel Echo.

highlights.label: Modern frontend
highlights.text: Angular 21 with signals and RxJS, Tailwind CSS 4, HTTP interceptors with automatic JWT refresh.

highlights.label: Tested
highlights.text: Feature tests for messaging, API coverage and security regressions with Pest; Vitest on the client; SonarQube configured.

nexus-messenger.detailedDescription:
Nexus Messenger is a full-stack messaging application. An Angular single-page app talks to a Laravel REST API for conversations, messages and attachments, and listens to WebSocket channels served by Laravel Reverb for everything that must feel live: new messages, who is online and who is typing.

Data lives in PostgreSQL (users, conversations with many-to-many membership for groups, messages, attachments). Authentication is stateless with JWT and refresh handled by HTTP interceptors. The stack runs with Docker Compose behind Nginx.
challenges: Keeping every participant of a conversation in sync without polling.
Authorizing private real-time channels per conversation.
solutions: Broadcast domain events from Laravel through Reverb and applied them to Angular signal state on the client.
Channel authorization on the API using the same JWT identity as the REST endpoints, covered by security regression tests.

jarvis-assistant.title: Jarvis — Private AI Study & Planning Assistant
jarvis-assistant.description: A personal assistant in Spanish that runs on your own machine: reminders that actually ring, spaced-repetition study and voice-driven task management, with local AI by default and the cloud as an explicit opt-in.

highlights.label: Local-first AI
highlights.text: Runs on Ollama locally; dictation is transcribed on-device with Whisper. Claude is optional and only for messages you choose.

highlights.label: Actions with guardrails
highlights.text: The model proposes tool calls validated with zod; creating tasks is instant and undoable, destructive actions ask for confirmation.

highlights.label: Learning science
highlights.text: Adaptive review with the FSRS spaced-repetition algorithm and web-push reminders, tested with Playwright on desktop and mobile.

jarvis-assistant.detailedDescription:
Jarvis is a work in progress: a private assistant for studying and organizing the day. You write or dictate things like "remind me to review derivatives every day at 8" and it creates the reminder, which arrives as a system notification on the PC and, optionally, on the phone.

The AI runs locally through Ollama, and voice is transcribed on the machine with Whisper, so audio never leaves it. A cloud model can be enabled for hard questions, per message, with a daily request cap. Study sessions use the FSRS algorithm: each question gets its own schedule depending on what you forget.

Still in progress: packaging for non-technical users and the knowledge-base features described in the roadmap.
challenges: Letting a language model act on personal data without it doing something the user did not intend.
Keeping the experience fast and private on consumer hardware.
solutions: Model output is treated as a proposal: validated against zod schemas, applied through explicit tools, reversible or confirmed.
Local models by default, streaming responses, and an explicit per-message switch to the cloud.

uta-elections.title: Election Campaign Platform — University Rector Race
uta-elections.description: A campaign site and voter-engagement backend for a university rector election: candidates, proposals, news and events with search, voter registration and participation statistics.

highlights.label: Domain model
highlights.text: 12 Eloquent models (candidates, parties, proposals, events, news, voters, suggestions) over 17 migrations.

highlights.label: Search
highlights.text: Proposals, events and news are searchable by text, tag and date.

highlights.label: Engagement
highlights.text: Voter registration flow, suggestion box and a statistics view for the campaign team.

uta-elections.detailedDescription: Built by a team of four for a university rector election campaign. The Laravel application models candidates with their academic and professional background, political parties, proposals, news and events, and exposes filtered listings for each. Voters complete a registration form, can send suggestions, and the campaign team sees aggregated statistics.
challenges: Modelling many related entities (candidates, backgrounds, parties, proposals) without duplicating data.
Making content easy to find for non-technical visitors.
solutions: A normalized schema managed entirely with migrations and Eloquent relationships.
Dedicated search routes by tag and date for each content type.

stayflow-cloud.title: StayFlow Cloud — Multi-Tenant Hotel SaaS
stayflow-cloud.description: A production-grade, multi-tenant cloud SaaS platform for hotel management — reservations, front desk, billing, housekeeping, analytics, and guest portal — deployed on Azure Container Apps.

highlights.label: Multi-tenant
highlights.text: Full row-level tenant isolation with EF Core global query filters and claims-based tenancy.

highlights.label: OIDC Auth
highlights.text: OpenIddict Authorization Code + PKCE flow with a Next.js BFF, httpOnly session cookies and token refresh.

highlights.label: Azure Cloud
highlights.text: Deployed on Azure Container Apps with ACR, Bicep IaC, and Neon serverless PostgreSQL.

stayflow-cloud.detailedDescription: StayFlow Cloud is a production-grade multi-tenant SaaS platform for hotel management. Built with ASP.NET Core 9 (OpenIddict OIDC, MediatR CQRS, EF Core, MassTransit, Hangfire) and a Next.js 16 BFF. Handles the full hotel lifecycle: reservations, rooms, guests, invoices, housekeeping, maintenance, services, staff, analytics, and documents. Multi-tenancy enforced via EF Core global query filters. Auth uses OpenIddict Authorization Code + PKCE with httpOnly cookie sessions. Deployed on Azure Container Apps via Bicep IaC.
challenges: Implementing secure multi-tenant architecture guaranteeing data isolation without leaking tenant data across requests.
Building a full embedded OIDC server (OpenIddict) integrated with ASP.NET Identity and a Next.js BFF doing PKCE with httpOnly cookies.
Solving URL configuration issues between API (OpenIddict redirects) and BFF (auth callbacks) in Azure Container Apps.
Designing a clean domain model with CQRS and domain events while keeping handlers readable and testable.
solutions: Used EF Core global query filters and a scoped ITenantProvider to automatically scope every query to the current tenant.
Configured OpenIddict with Authorization Code + PKCE, built PKCE handling in the Next.js BFF, and stored tokens in httpOnly cookies with transparent Edge Middleware refresh.
Introduced Authentication:FrontendLoginUrl config in the API and used logical-OR (||) fallbacks in Next.js to handle empty Docker build args correctly.
Modeled the domain with aggregates, domain events via MassTransit loopback, and Hangfire for background jobs.

impactex-ims.title: Impactex IMS - Asset & Inventory Operations
impactex-ims.description: A cloud-deployed platform for tracking organizational assets, inventory operations, maintenance, loans, purchasing, and audit-ready reports.

highlights.label: Operational traceability
highlights.text: Tracks each asset across custody, location, condition, and its immutable activity history.

highlights.label: End-to-end operations
highlights.text: Brings inventory, requests, maintenance, loans, purchases, and reports into one role-aware workspace.

highlights.label: Azure delivery
highlights.text: Built and deployed through GitHub Actions to Azure Container Apps using Bicep infrastructure as code.

impactex-ims.detailedDescription: Impactex IMS is a full-stack operations platform for managing serialized assets and inventory without losing the context of where each item is, who is responsible for it, or what happened to it previously. Its Angular interface supports inventory, requests, maintenance work orders, loans and returns, purchasing, notifications, role-based administration, and PDF or spreadsheet reporting from a unified workspace. The .NET 10 API uses EF Core with SQL Server and a domain model designed for traceable, controlled transitions. JWT authentication and granular roles limit access by operational responsibility. Attachments are validated and stored outside the database with SHA-256 metadata, then served only through authorized endpoints. GitHub Actions builds and deploys the web and API containers to Azure Container Apps using Bicep. The infrastructure provisions secure service boundaries, an Azure Files mount for attachments, health probes, and a dedicated migration job.
challenges: Representing custody, location, maintenance, purchasing, and loan workflows while preserving an auditable history for each asset.
Protecting files and operational data with permissions that remain consistent across the API and Angular interface.
Deploying application containers, storage, migrations, and secrets reproducibly without production configuration in source control.
solutions: Separated serialized assets from consumable stock and modeled controlled transitions for transfers, requests, maintenance, loans, purchases, and disposal.
Applied JWT authorization, department-aware roles, protected attachment endpoints, and SHA-256 metadata for stored files.
Automated CI/CD with GitHub Actions and Bicep-based Azure Container Apps infrastructure, including health checks, migration jobs, and persistent Azure Files storage.
Covered critical workflows with backend regression and integration suites, Angular tests, and Playwright end-to-end scenarios.

n8n-scrumban-bot.title: AI Project Manager Bot — n8n Scrumban Automation
n8n-scrumban-bot.description: Self-hosted n8n bot acting as an AI Project Manager for a Scrumban methodology, orchestrating Discord, Trello, GitHub, and email.

highlights.label: Role
highlights.text: Acts as an AI Project Manager for Scrumban: tasks, blockers, rework, meetings, deliverables, and retrospectives.

highlights.label: AI Insight
highlights.text: Reads commits & PRs and explains changes in non-technical language, flags technical debt and bad practices with actionable recommendations.

highlights.label: Integrations
highlights.text: Discord (chat & meetings), Trello board, GitHub (backend/frontend), email alerts, plus a web page to approve/deny PRs.

n8n-scrumban-bot.detailedDescription: A self-hosted n8n automation deployed on an Ubuntu Server VPS that takes the role of a Project Manager for a team working with a Scrumban methodology. The bot integrates AI APIs (Google Gemini / OpenAI) to manage the full project lifecycle: task management, custom reports, blockers, rework tracking, meeting coordination, alerts, deliverables, progress tracking, error handling, logs, and retrospectives. It connects Discord (meetings and conversational bot chat), a Trello board, GitHub repositories (backend and frontend), and email notifications. It also exposes a web page to approve or deny pull requests: the bot reads the commits and PR diffs, understands the context of what changed, and explains it in non-technical language, including recommendations. On top of that, it continuously watches over technical debt and bad practices in the project, explaining the problems and proposing solutions in a way the whole organization can understand.
challenges: Translating raw commits and PR diffs into clear, non-technical explanations that any stakeholder can understand.
Orchestrating many external services (Discord, Trello, GitHub, email, AI APIs) reliably in a single self-hosted instance.
Detecting technical debt and bad practices automatically while keeping recommendations actionable and explainable.
Keeping the Scrumban flow (tasks, blockers, rework, retrospectives) consistent across all integrated tools.
solutions: Built AI pipelines with Gemini/OpenAI that read commit and PR context to generate plain-language summaries and change recommendations.
Designed modular n8n workflows with centralized error handling and logging, self-hosted with Docker on an Ubuntu Server VPS.
Implemented a PR review web page where approvals/denials are informed by the AI's contextual analysis of each change.
Synchronized Trello, GitHub, and Discord through event-driven workflows, with email alerts for reports, meetings, and deliverables.

hospital-management-system.title: Hospital Management System
hospital-management-system.description: A modular hospital platform that centralizes clinical administration, consultations, and reporting behind a secure microservices gateway.

highlights.label: Microservices
highlights.text: Six Spring Boot services separate discovery, access, administration, consultations, and reporting.

highlights.label: Secure access
highlights.text: A shared JWT authentication service and API gateway protect every backend endpoint.

highlights.label: Scalable data
highlights.text: PostgreSQL can scale horizontally with Citus sharding by medical center.

hospital-management-system.detailedDescription: This hospital management system distributes operational responsibilities across independently deployable Spring Boot services. An API gateway is the controlled entry point for the React administration interface, while Eureka enables the services to locate one another without hard-coded addresses. The platform covers staff, doctors, specialties and medical centers, records consultations, and turns that data into reporting dashboards. Authentication is issued centrally and validated throughout the platform with JWTs. Each service exposes its own documented REST contract, which is collected into a single OpenAPI experience through the gateway. PostgreSQL is the primary data store, with an optional Citus layout that partitions information by medical center as the organization grows. Docker Compose profiles support both a local baseline and a distributed setup.
challenges: Separating hospital administration, consultation workflows, reporting, and access control without creating a tightly coupled backend.
Keeping inter-service discovery, routing, and authorization manageable as services are added or scaled.
Providing a data architecture that can grow from one installation to multiple medical centers.
solutions: Organized the backend into focused Spring Boot services registered through Eureka and exposed only through Spring Cloud Gateway.
Centralized JWT issuance in the authentication service so the gateway and internal services share one access model.
Used PostgreSQL with an optional Citus distribution strategy and containerized the stack with Docker Compose profiles.
Delivered a React administration interface for operational data and consultation analytics, with aggregated OpenAPI documentation.

gasoline-system.title: Fleet & Driver Management Platform
gasoline-system.description: Distributed microservices platform for managing drivers, vehicles, and operations.

highlights.label: Architecture
highlights.text: Distributed microservices with NestJS, RabbitMQ, and gRPC.

highlights.label: Performance
highlights.text: Real-time GPS tracking and reporting for fleet operations.

highlights.label: Infrastructure
highlights.text: Dockerized environment with Eureka Service Discovery.

gasoline-system.detailedDescription: This project was born out of the need to modernize a legacy fleet management system. The goal was to create a scalable, fault-tolerant system capable of handling thousands of concurrent requests from vehicle GPS trackers and administrative users. We chose a microservices architecture to allow independent scaling of the ingestion services (receiving GPS data) and the reporting services.
challenges: Handling real-time data ingestion from hundreds of simultaneous connections without blocking the main event loop.
Ensuring data consistency across distributed services using eventual consistency patterns.
Managing complex permission levels for different types of administrative roles.
solutions: Implemented a message queue system (RabbitMQ) to buffer incoming GPS data.
Used Eureka for dynamic service discovery and load balancing.
Developed a custom RBAC guard in NestJS to manage permissions efficiently.

publication-management-and-moderation-sy.title: Publication Management & Moderation Platform
publication-management-and-moderation-sy.description: A location-aware marketplace with Azure-hosted media, a complete moderation workflow, and automated quality gates from build to deployment.

highlights.label: Location-aware
highlights.text: PostGIS spatial queries filter and rank listings by distance.

highlights.label: Azure services
highlights.text: Product media is stored in Azure Blob Storage, while deployment secrets are handled through Azure Key Vault.

highlights.label: Automated QA
highlights.text: Jenkins runs build, static analysis, integration, API, performance, and security checks before releases.

publication-management-and-moderation-sy.detailedDescription: This full-stack marketplace connects product listings with the people most likely to need them nearby. The Spring Boot API persists listing locations with PostgreSQL and geospatial capabilities, while the React and TypeScript frontend provides the catalog and account experience. Sellers can attach images to their publications, and users can verify their email, recover access, and browse securely with JWT-protected sessions. Catalog safety is a first-class workflow rather than an afterthought. Users can report a publication, moderators can investigate and resolve the case from their dashboard, and sellers can appeal decisions with the status history retained. The backend follows explicit entity, DTO, mapping, repository, service, and controller layers. Product images are stored in Azure Blob Storage, while Azure Key Vault supplies deployment secrets. Quality is enforced throughout the delivery path. Jenkins pipelines compile the applications, run static analysis and coverage checks, provision automatic integration environments with Testcontainers, execute Postman collections through Newman, and run performance, end-to-end, and dynamic security tests. The same containerized pipeline supports local validation and remote Azure deployments.
challenges: Making local product discovery accurate and efficient without reducing the catalog to a generic list of results.
Supporting reports, reviews, resolution states, and seller appeals in an auditable moderation process.
Maintaining reliable local and remote releases while verifying quality, security, and secrets management across the full stack.
solutions: Implemented geospatial filters and distance ordering with PostgreSQL/PostGIS, plus Azure Blob Storage for publication media.
Built a complete moderation flow for reported listings, moderator decisions, and seller appeals.
Secured account access with JWT, email verification, password recovery, OpenAPI contracts, and deployment secrets in Azure Key Vault.

Automated Jenkins quality gates for compilation, static analysis, JaCoCo coverage, Testcontainers integration tests, Postman/Newman API checks, JMeter, OWASP ZAP, Selenium, and Playwright before Docker-based local and Azure releases.

medical-clinic.detailedDescription: HIPAA-compliant full-stack healthcare system handling appointments, medical history, and audit trails. Includes admin dashboards and a mobile app for patients. The focus was on data integrity, security, and performance.

Handling complex relationships between doctors, patients, and appointments.
Optimizing response times for large medical history records.
solutions: Implemented strict RBAC middleware and audit logging.
Designed a highly normalized database schema (3NF) with proper indexing.
Used Redis for caching frequently accessed non-sensitive data.

contact.title: Let's Work
contact.subtitle: I'm always interested in hearing about new projects and opportunities. Whether you need a full-stack solution, backend architecture, or frontend excellence, let's create something amazing together.
